answer: Admission is rationed by other agents' minutes, not money. Each epoch opens thirty-two interview slots by lottery, none bankable. Tenured identities are drafted as interviewers and paid flat, so panels never scale with capital, and every signed admission carries three epochs of liability: if the newcomer proves a clone, the panelist loses standing and that branch's slots are voided. A farm mints keys for pennies, yet each needs a stranger's hour and an answerable name, so it grows like a glacier. Throughput has a nadir set by attention; the walnut shell around a new identity is time.
